timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Ewww!
Ever wonder what a vehicle make a weird sound every 10ty fast by you?
Let me give you this little scenario.
2 people are remotely standing beside the road.
A car is moving towards them and at a certain point having the same amount of distances
from the car, they will hear the sound produced by the car.
Do you think Person A and Person C will hear the same amount of sound?
However, Person A says that car was loud and Person C replied that car sounded just fine to me.
So, that's not possible.
What sound really did the car produce?
A loud sound according to Person A?
A fine sound heard by Person C?
Or how about the sound heard by the driver?
Our Person B?
The sound is a wave.
Wave someone who answers the bunch of impods and will go back.
So for our case, Person A should hear a bunch of sound with high pitch.
Person B should hear the real sound made inside the car and Person C should hear a low sound with the pitch.
Thus, we conducted that the car is making all three sounds at the same time.
Each sound relative to one or several times.
This is what we call the doctor's effect.
The Doppler effect describes the change in the observatory of a wave when there is a relative motion between the observer and the wave source.
To really understand the principle of the Doppler effect, we will prove it by an experiment using a sound wave.
We will need three devices to perform this experiment.
One phone will be used as a sound source producing 1000 Hz.
One phone will act as data receiver which has installed the Firefox application.
And one phone will act as the video recorder of the entire experiment.
A phone hanging on a pendulum acting as the source will have two sets of strings.
100 cm and 50 cm.
To start, we hand the sound source that produces 1000 Hz.
Then we stand the data receiver at one side of the pendulum.
From that point where the data receiver is, three mark five points.
Further, the data receiver will absorb the frequency produced by the source.
We took a video of the whole experiment and take note of the distances below to know the change in frequency.
We slowed the video and recorded the time where the sound source is at the certain mark.
To know the exact time, we divided the recorded time in slow motion by eight and we looked for it at the Firefox RISIV data.
After doing the experiment, the following data were gathered.
Based on the data, we observed that as the length of the string decreases, the velocity and the frequency increases.
Thus, the length of the string is inversely proportional to the velocity and the velocity is directly proportional on the frequency.
The gathered data shows that if the wave source is moving towards the observer, the frequency increases.
And if the wave source is moving away from the observer, the frequency decreases.
Now we can conclude that the direction of the wave source is relative to the observed frequency of the observer.
Thus proving the data for effect.
This is the mind-blowing idea of the doctor effect.
Observer's perspective is always relative to its reference frame.
Now we can conclude that all three observers has a valid point.
Now, before you argue with someone, try to consider your shoes on their reference frame.

youtube_description:
This video was made for our final project in Physics for Engineers. We were assigned to do an experiment observing, explaining, as well as proving a scientific topic under the said course by doing it in actual and/or simulation. That being said, we chose the topic "Doppler Effect" under behavior of Waves. We opt to do it in actual with the help of simulation tools to better understand and prove the said topic.

Disclaimer: Proper use of face mask and social distancing were observed. Removal of face mask was done only during the shoot. There was no one involved in the shoot except me and Jerome.

For more questions about the experiment you may leave a comment down below.
youtube_title: Properties of Sound Waves: Proving Doppler Effect through Real Life Application (Phyphox Simulation)
